name: Neutral (not measured)
_note: Conservative defaults for any phone that has not been measured: high-pass 120 Hz, low-mid +2 dB at 220 Hz, treble -2 dB at 4.5 kHz, 3 dB of output headroom. The EQ start (2026-10-23, docs/SPEAKER_ESTIMATES.md) is the S26 Ultra shape scaled back to the weak end of 92 Android phones measured by NotebookCheck: 90 % of them are 10 dB down (re the mids) at or below about 240 Hz, and their 200-400 Hz band is at most about 2 dB below the S26 Ultra; datasheets and papers bound it from above (no part makes useful bass below its box resonance without the maker's processing). Match-on-disable is off, so the S26U-tuned loudness weighting of the matcher is never used; the S26U speaker and limiter curves are not shown. Virtual bass starts at +0, the weakest step (not +4 as on the S26U): nothing is known about an unmeasured speaker, so the default only switches it on and every increase is left to the listener; the EQ balance comes first (2026-10-23, S25+ feedback; the home tip says the same).
_devmode_note: Developer mode: speaker_floor_hz (graph zone below which the speaker plays practically nothing) and the bass protection threshold line protect_db_at_50 + protect_db_per_pct x (volume % - 50), at our output, 150-400 Hz, sine-equivalent dBFS. Not measured on this phone: the S26U line, shown as an estimate.
